sourcedFrom: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) (2022)
cleanIntro: The book for this can is JK Armament's 195, 155 & 105 Series Operation and Maintenance Manual, where it is the 155 RPX .45CAL, with a section of its own. It ships with the 155 LT quick attach taper mount, a 2.5 inch tube, one 155 PRO blast baffle, seven 155 LT modular baffles and the 155 LT flash cut end cap, all threaded together. It is a modular can, not a sealed one. JK's maintenance is short and the same for every can in the book: unthread each component, clean with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush, inspect, and thread it back together hand tight.

steps.title: Host unloaded and the action open first
steps.action: Before the can comes off, unload the host and open the action so you can see it is clear of ammunition. If you are not sure how to do that on your firearm, its own manual is the authority.
steps.prose: This guide is for the suppressor. The host's own book is the authority on clearing the host.
steps.quote: WARNING: Before removing the suppressor from the host firearm, be sure the firearm is unloaded and the action is opened so it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 2.0 Installation, p.3

steps.title: It may be hot — gloves
steps.action: A can that has just been fired can burn you. Let it cool, or take it off in heat-resistant gloves, as JK directs.
steps.prose: The RPX .45CAL is rated for full-auto on pistol calibers and 300 Blackout, so it can be run very hot.
steps.quote: When removing the suppressor, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing. Use heat-resistant gloves to avoid burns or other injuries.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 2.0 Installation, p.3

steps.title: What it is rated for
steps.action: JK rates the RPX .45CAL for full-auto on 9mm, 45 ACP, 40 S&W, 10mm and every .45 caliber and smaller pistol cartridge, and on 300 Blackout, with no minimum barrel length. Every other caliber in JK's table carries a minimum barrel length (8.6 Blackout only when supersonic), and 5.56, 7.62x39, 243, 308, 6.5 Creedmoor, 7mm Rem Mag and 300 Win Mag are rated for sporting use only.
steps.prose: The big-bore rounds in JK's table are rated full-auto from a minimum barrel: 450 Bushmaster and 458 SOCOM from 8 inches, 350 Legend, 45-70 and 450 Marlin from 16 inches. 8.6 Blackout needs no minimum subsonic and 12.5 inches supersonic.
steps.quote: JK 155 RPX .45CAL is rated for full-auto use on many pistol calibers, plus 300 BLK, with no barrel length restrictions. It is rated for sporting use on rifle calibers.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 3.2 JK 155 RPX .45CAL — Barrel and Caliber Ratings, p.7

steps.title: Sporting use means ten rounds, then cool
steps.action: On the calibers JK rates for sporting use, fire ten rounds and then let the can cool to ambient temperature before the next string.
steps.prose: JK also notes that suppressor life is significantly reduced in high-heat use on short-barrelled rifles.
steps.quote: Sporting use is defined as 10 rounds of fire, followed by cooling to ambient temperature.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 3.2 JK 155 RPX .45CAL — Barrel and Caliber Ratings, p.7
steps.warn: Sporting-rated calibers: ten rounds, then cool to ambient — and observe JK's minimum barrel lengths.

steps.title: Off the host
steps.action: Take the can off the host. It ships on the 155 LT quick attach taper mount, JK's mount for its own muzzle devices; direct thread mounts are sold separately. Once it is off, JK recommends a thread protector or another muzzle device on the barrel to protect the threads and crown.
steps.prose: Every 155 Series mount uses the same 1.375-24 tube thread, so the mount you have is the one that goes back on.
steps.quote: The JK 155 system includes a Quick Attach Taper Mount, which is designed for use with our muzzle device options.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 2.0 Installation, p.3

steps.title: Unthread each component
steps.action: Unthread the mount, the tube and the end cap, and take out the 155 PRO blast baffle and the seven 155 LT modular baffles. Do it by hand where you can; JK allows a JK 155 series wrench if needed, or a crescent or combination wrench.
steps.prose: Lay the parts out in the order they came off, and keep the one PRO blast baffle apart from the seven LT modular baffles. The book prints no stacking diagram, so your own layout is the record of how it goes back.
steps.quote: Unthread each component. Use a JK 155 or JK 105 series wrench to disassemble, if necessary. A crescent wrench or a combination wrench may also be used.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance — Disassembly, p.25

steps.title: Thread locker means heat first
steps.action: If Blue Loctite or another removable thread locker was used on any joint, that joint may need heating before it will come apart. Do not force it with the wrench cold.
steps.prose: Carbon can lock a joint on its own too; a wrench on a joint that will not turn is how threads get galled.
steps.quote: CAUTION: If Blue Loctite® or other removable thread locker was used, the unit may need to be heated prior to disassembly.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance — Disassembly, p.25
steps.warn: Never crank a locked joint cold — heat first.

steps.title: Ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush
steps.action: Clean every component with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush. That is JK's whole method for this can — nothing harsher is named.
steps.prose: The can is grade 5 titanium and 7075 aluminium under hard anodize and Cerakote, so a nylon brush, not steel.
steps.quote: JK Armament recommends cleaning your Mission Configurable Suppressor using CLP (ammonia free) and a nylon brush.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance, p.25

steps.title: Lead — protect yourself and dispose of it properly
steps.action: Expect lead and other toxic residue inside the can. Gloves on, clean away from food, and dispose of the dirty CLP and rags properly.
steps.prose: Primer residue carries lead even when the bullets are jacketed.
steps.quote: Lead and other toxic materials may be deposited inside of your suppressor; use appropriate cautions and disposal methods when cleaning.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance, p.25

steps.title: Carbon off every thread and face
steps.action: Brush the carbon off the threads and the faces of every component — the mount, both ends of the tube, the end cap and each baffle face.
steps.prose: Carbon on a thread or a face is what stops a joint closing fully and what makes it seize next time.
steps.quote: Keep carbon deposits off of threads and faces of all components.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance, p.25

steps.title: Inspect every component and thread
steps.action: With everything clean, look at each component and each thread before anything goes back together.
steps.prose: A damaged thread, a cracked or bent baffle, or a dented tube does not go back in. JK's warranty and repair route is through its online RMA form.
steps.quote: Clean all components with an appropriate CLP (ammonia free) and a nylon brush. Inspect all components and threads.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 4.0 Maintenance — Disassembly, p.25

steps.title: Clear and dry before it is fired
steps.action: Look through the bore: nothing in it. JK forbids firing through an obstructed suppressor, and a can that has been under water must drain completely first.
steps.prose: Mud, dirt or a rag fibre in the bore is an obstruction.
steps.quote: DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed suppressor. If submerged in water, the user must allow sufficient time to drain the suppressor completely.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 2.0 Installation, p.2
steps.warn: Never fire through an obstructed suppressor.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You should have the can off the host and apart: the taper mount, tube, the 155 PRO blast baffle, seven 155 LT modular baffles and the end cap, each cleaned and inspected. Reassembly is next.
steps.prose: That is everything JK's book takes apart.
steps.cite: JK ARMAMENT™ 195, 155, & 105 SERIES OPERATION AND MAINTENANCE MANUAL — ISSUED: Sept 1st, 2022 (p.1) — 3.2 JK 155 RPX .45CAL — Includes, p.6

deepAbsentReason: There is no deeper clean for the 155 RPX .45CAL. JK's maintenance section (p.25) gives one disassembly for every can in the book — unthread each component, clean with ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush, inspect — and that is the field strip above. The book takes no component further apart and describes no other cleaning method.

cleaning.name: BAFFLES, TUBE & END CAP
tasks: The 155 PRO blast baffle, seven 155 LT modular baffles, the tube and the end cap
Ammonia-free CLP and a nylon brush — JK's method
Do not use a cleaner containing ammonia
Gloves on: lead and other toxic residue; dispose of dirty CLP and rags properly

cleaning.name: THREADS & FACES
tasks: Carbon brushed off every component face

cleaning.name: MOUNT
tasks: The 155 LT taper mount cleaned and its tube threads inspected
The host's muzzle device or barrel threads and shoulder cleaned so the mount seats fully

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: A can that was wet is drained completely
A thread protector or muzzle device on the host's barrel while the can is off

reassembly: Apply a light coat of CLP to the threads and inspect every component and thread before assembling.
Thread the components back together in the order you laid them out, taking care not to cross thread, with the flash cut end cap last.
Hand tighten the components together. If you use a torque setting, do not exceed 10 ft/lbs; one drop of Blue 242 Loctite may be used for a more robust configuration.
Fit the can to the host so the mount is fully shouldered, with no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the thread mount or muzzle device. Never use a crush washer.
Check the can is still secure after 30 rounds, and keep checking it often.
fncheck: Look through the bore: clear. The caliber and barrel length you will shoot are ones JK's table rates for the RPX .45CAL. The mount sits fully shouldered with no visible gap and no crush washer. Every joint is hand tight with no cross threading, and the can is checked again for tightness after 30 rounds.
